key_insight: ROS-LLM is an open-source ROS framework that lets non-experts control robots using large language models, learn new skills from demonstrations and feedback, and automatically tune actions for reliable real-world performance.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between powerful LLM reasoning and practical robot control by making language-guided skill acquisition, human-in-the-loop refinement, and deployment-level action tuning accessible to researchers and practitioners without deep robotics expertise.
method: Modular ROS integration that connects LLMs to perception, planning, and control nodes so language can drive embodied actions.
Learning-from-demonstration and human-feedback pipeline that converts demonstrations and corrections into executable robot skills.
Automatic action-parameter tuning and closed-loop verification to improve robustness and reliability in real-world task execution.
impact: Lowers the barrier for deploying LLM-guided behaviors on robots, speeding prototyping and reproducible experimentation. Improves reliability of language-driven robotic systems, making them more usable outside research labs.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: ROS nodes (perception, LLM, planner, controller) and data flow arrows showing language→action loop.
Pipeline flowchart: demonstration → LLM interpretation → skill synthesis → tuning → deployment.
Before/after reliability chart: task success rate or error rate comparing manual tuning vs ROS-LLM automatic tuning.
User journey icon set: non-expert issues natural language command, provides a demo/feedback, robot executes refined behavior.
paper_title: A robot operating system framework for using large language models in embodied AI
paper_authors: Christopher E. Mower, Yuhui Wan, Hongzhan Yu, Antoine Grosnit, Jonas Gonzalez-Billandon
